syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

concepts.learning_objective: Identify India's latitudinal extent, its southern limit and the extent of its territorial waters.
Explain why India's north-south distance exceeds its east-west distance despite similar degree extents.
Explain how India's position across tropical and sub-tropical zones causes physical diversity.

topics.title: Longitude, time and the standard meridian

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate and interpret the local time difference arising from India's longitudinal extent.
Explain the choice of 82°30' E as the standard meridian and the relation of IST to GMT.
Recall India's area, its share of world land surface and its rank by size.
Explain how India's size and peninsular shape provide physical diversity and a long coastline.
Describe the countries of the Indian subcontinent and the role of the Himalayas as a barrier.
Describe India's location in south-central Asia and the advantages of its maritime position.
Identify India's land and island neighbours and the water bodies separating them.

topics.title: Geological divisions and the Peninsular Block

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the three geological divisions of India and the forces that shaped them.
Describe the boundary, rock composition and stability of the Peninsular Block.

topics.title: The Himalayas and the Indo-Ganga-Brahmaputra Plain as geological divisions
topics.ncert_sections: The Himalayas and other Peninsular mountains; Indo-Ganga-Brahmaputra Plain

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the Himalayas are young, weak and flexible and what landforms show their youthful rivers.
Describe the origin of the Indo-Ganga-Brahmaputra Plain from a geosynclinal depression.
State the main Himalayan ranges, their dimensions and changing orientation across India.
Evaluate the role of the Himalayas as a physical, climatic, drainage and cultural divide.
Distinguish the Bhabar, Tarai, Bhangar and Khadar zones of the northern plains.
Explain the mature-stage fluvial landforms, deltas and water divides of the northern plains.

topics.title: The Peninsular Plateau
topics.ncert_sections: The Peninsular Plateau; The Deccan Plateau; The Central Highlands; The Northeastern Plateau

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the extent, elevation and characteristic landforms of the Peninsular plateau.
Compare the Western and Eastern Ghats and locate the main peaks of the Deccan plateau.
Explain the features of the Central Highlands and the origin of the Meghalaya plateau.
Identify the climate and wind-formed landforms of the Indian desert.
Interpret the evidence that the desert region was once under the sea.
Explain why the western coastal plain is narrow, deltaless and rich in natural ports.
Explain the features of the broad, emergent eastern coastal plain.
Describe the location, origin and features of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
Describe the location, coral origin and features of the Lakshadweep and Minicoy islands.

topics.title: Drainage, drainage basins and drainage patterns

concepts.learning_objective: Define drainage, catchment area, drainage basin and watershed and distinguish a river basin from a watershed.
Identify dendritic, radial, trellis and centripetal drainage patterns with examples.

topics.title: Classification of the Indian drainage system

concepts.learning_objective: Classify Indian drainage into the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal drainage and name the water divide between them.
Classify Indian river basins as major, medium and minor on the basis of catchment area.
Explain the basis and limitation of classifying Indian drainage into Himalayan and Peninsular drainage.

topics.title: The Himalayan drainage and its evolution

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the erosional and depositional features and the perennial nature of Himalayan rivers.
Explain the Indo-Brahma hypothesis and the events that dismembered it into three river systems.
Describe the source, course and right bank tributaries of the Indus.
Identify the five rivers of the Panjnad and their key features.
Describe the source, course and important tributaries of the Ganga.
Describe the course, names and tributaries of the Brahmaputra and its flood problems.
Explain the characteristics of Peninsular rivers and the geological events that shaped them.
Identify the major east-flowing and west-flowing Peninsular rivers and their features.

topics.title: Extent of usability of river water

concepts.learning_objective: Evaluate problems in using river water, including uneven flow, pollution and inter-basin transfer.

topics.title: Unity and Diversity in the Monsoon Climate

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish weather as the momentary state of the atmosphere from climate as long-period average conditions.
Describe regional variations in temperature and precipitation within India's monsoon climate.

topics.title: Factors Determining the Climate of India

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how latitude, the Himalayas and the distribution of land and water control India's climate.
Explain the effect of distance from the sea, altitude and relief on temperature and rainfall.
Explain the onset of the monsoon through differential heating, the northward shift of the ITCZ and jet streams.
Explain the causes of breaks in the monsoon in different regions.
Describe El Nino and the Southern Oscillation and their use in monsoon forecasting.
Explain the causes of excessive cold in north India and the mild winter of the Peninsula.
Describe pressure, winds and the sources of winter rainfall in India.
Describe the northward shift of the heat belt and the position of the ITCZ in summer.
Identify the local storms of the hot weather season and their effects.

topics.title: The Southwest Monsoon and Retreating Monsoon Seasons

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal branches of the southwest monsoon and the rainfall they cause.
Describe the retreating monsoon, October heat and cyclonic rainfall on the east coast.

topics.title: Traditional Seasons, Rainfall Distribution and Economic Life

concepts.learning_objective: Match the six traditional Indian seasons with their months.
Classify regions of India by annual rainfall.
Evaluate the role of the monsoon in India's agriculture and economic life.
Explain the role of greenhouse gases and human activities in global warming.
Predict the effects of global warming such as sea-level rise and shifting climatic boundaries.

topics.title: Natural Vegetation and Tropical Evergreen and Semi Evergreen Forests
topics.ncert_sections: Introduction; Types of Forests; Tropical Evergreen and Semi Evergreen Forests

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what natural vegetation is and how it differs from planted vegetation.
Describe the climate, distribution, structure and species of tropical evergreen and semi evergreen forests.
Explain how British commercial exploitation changed the structure of Indian forests.

topics.title: Tropical Deciduous and Tropical Thorn Forests
topics.ncert_sections: Tropical Deciduous Forests; Tropical Thorn Forests

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish moist and dry deciduous forests by rainfall, distribution and species.
Describe the rainfall conditions, areas and species of tropical thorn forests.
Relate the change in Himalayan vegetation to altitude and slope aspect.
Describe the southern mountain forests including the Sholas.
Identify the extent, categories and Ramsar sites of India's wetlands.
Describe where mangroves grow in India and why they need conservation.

topics.title: Forest Conservation and Social Forestry
topics.ncert_sections: Forest Conservation; Forests and Life; Social Forestry; Farm Forestry

concepts.learning_objective: State the aims of India's forest policy of 1952 as modified in 1988.
Distinguish urban, rural (agro and community) and farm forestry.
Explain the role of forests in tribal life and of tribals in conservation.

topics.title: Wildlife and Its Conservation
topics.ncert_sections: Wildlife; Wildlife Conservation in India; Biosphere Reserves

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the causes of the decline of wildlife in India.
Describe the Wildlife Act of 1972 and projects such as Project Tiger and Project Elephant.
Explain the concept of a Biosphere Reserve and identify India's Biosphere Reserves.

topics.title: Disasters and natural hazards: meaning and changing perception

concepts.learning_objective: State the meaning of a disaster and identify disasters caused directly or indirectly by human actions.
Distinguish a natural hazard from a natural disaster and explain when a hazard becomes a disaster.
Explain how intensified human activity in hazard-prone areas has increased vulnerability.

topics.title: Classification of natural disasters and international efforts

concepts.learning_objective: Classify natural disasters as atmospheric, terrestrial, aquatic or biological.
Describe the Yokohama Strategy (1994) and the International Decade for Natural Disaster Reduction.
Explain why the Himalayan arc and parts of the Peninsula experience earthquakes.
Identify the earthquake damage risk zones of India and the regions in them.
Describe the effects of earthquakes and the preparedness measures to mitigate them.
Explain how tsunamis form and why their height increases in shallow coastal water.
Explain why tsunami losses are large and why mitigation needs international cooperation.
State the initial conditions needed for the formation of a tropical cyclone.
Describe where and when tropical cyclones originate around India.
Explain the consequences of tropical cyclones, including storm surge.
Explain the natural and human causes of floods.
Identify the flood-prone states of India and the types of flooding they face.
Evaluate the consequences of floods and the measures to control them.
Distinguish meteorological, agricultural, hydrological and ecological droughts.
Identify the extreme, severe and moderate drought-affected areas of India.
Explain the consequences of drought and its immediate and long-term mitigation measures.
Identify the landslide vulnerability zones of India and the factors controlling landslides.
Explain the consequences of landslides and area-specific mitigation measures.
Describe pre-disaster, during-disaster and post-disaster management stages.
